title: Shree 420
writers: Khwaja Ahmad Abbas; V. P. Sathe
research_notes: Filmography notes: Child artist; Guest appearance in the song "Pyar Hua Iqrar Hua". Infobox gross '₹3.9 crore' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. A child appearance at roughly three years old, in the song 'Pyar Hua Iqrar Hua' in his father Raj Kapoor's film. The filmography table gives the role as 'Himself' but notes 'Child artist'; it is a child role, not a self appearance. The main Rishi Kapoor article's career section garbles this, appending 'and earned him the Filmfare Award for Best Actor' to the sentence about this cameo, which cannot be right for a three-year-old's walk-on; the claim is not carried over. Box office now entered from the article's labelled figures: ₹3.9 crore gross and ₹2 crore nett in India in 1955, superseding the phase-1 decision to omit the unlabelled infobox gross. The article also reports roughly 35 million Indian admissions and a Soviet release of 8.75 million roubles on about 35 million tickets; the Soviet amount is in a different currency and is not combined into a worldwide figure. Romance centrality reflects the Raj-Vidya romance, which is central to the film; Kapoor's own walk-on has no romantic content, so romance presence is None.
role_gist: Kapoor's first time on screen, at roughly three years old, as one of the children who pass Raj and Vidya under the umbrella during 'Pyar Hua Iqrar Hua'. He has no character, no dialogue and no bearing on the plot; the filmography table lists the credit as 'Himself' but flags it as a child-artist appearance, and it is better read as a walk-on than as a role.
recognition: One of the most widely seen Indian films of its era, with a very large Soviet release; the song Kapoor walks through is among the best known in Hindi cinema.

title: Mera Naam Joker
lyricist: Neeraj; Shailendra; Hasrat Jaipuri; Prem Dhawan
research_notes: Filmography notes: Child artist. Infobox gross 'US$22 million (USSR)' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. His credited debut, as the adolescent Raju, for which he won the National Film Award for Best Child Artist. Kapoor plays the young Raju in Chapter I only; the adult Raju is Raj Kapoor. The romance scored here is the Raju-Mary thread, which is the whole of Kapoor's segment, so romance presence is Major for his part even though the film as a whole distributes its romances across three women and three chapters.
character_social_background: Poor; lives with his widowed mother near a private Christian school he attends on sufferance
role_gist: Kapoor's credited debut, playing the adolescent Raju in the film's first chapter. A chubby, clumsy sixteen-year-old known as the class clown, he conceives an overwhelming first love for his teacher Mary, learns that his dead father was a circus clown and resolves to become one, and is expelled after being seen clowning for money in the street. He gives Mary a toy clown and stands as best man at her wedding.
principal_motivation: To be loved by Mary, and to become the clown his father was.
principal_conflict: A boy's first love directed at a grown woman who cannot return it, against a mother who dreads the circus.
character_arc: From a boy who makes others laugh to hide his own poverty to one who learns that the laughter will have to cover grief as well.
character_outcome: Loses Mary to David, attends the wedding as best man, and is given the toy clown back.
recognition: Won Kapoor the National Film Award for Best Child Artist. The film failed on release and was later reassessed as a cult classic and among Raj Kapoor's best.
critical_reception: A commercial failure on release; the article records that it later came to be considered a cult classic and one of Raj Kapoor's best films.

title: Bobby
writers: Jainendra Jain; Khwaja Ahmad Abbas; V. P. Sathe
research_notes: Infobox gross '₹31 crore' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Highest-grossing Indian film of 1973 at ₹11 crore in India, given by the article as a gross. Adjusted figures of ₹398 crore in 2011 value are reported but are not entered, since inflation adjustment was not requested. Soviet admissions and rouble takings are recorded separately and not combined into a worldwide total.
character_occupation: Student, recently home from boarding school
character_social_background: Only son of the rich Hindu businessman Ram Nath; raised by servants and a governess rather than by his parents
role_gist: Raj returns from boarding school into a house where his parents have no time for him, and falls in love at first sight with Bobby Braganza, the granddaughter of his old governess. The film is built almost wholly on his pursuit of her and his revolt against a father who despises her family's poverty and faith, ending in a flight, a chase and a near-drowning before the fathers relent.
principal_motivation: To marry Bobby against his father's absolute refusal.
principal_conflict: A rich Hindu father and a poor Goan Christian father, each insulting the other, between him and the girl.
character_arc: From a neglected and lonely boy to one willing to leave his family and his money for a girl his father has forbidden him.
character_outcome: Reunited with Bobby after the elopement collapses and both fathers give way.
critical_reception: The article cites a contemporary review crediting the film's commercial appeal to its two fresh-faced young leads and praising the pair for acting with natural ease and freshness.
recognition: The film that made Kapoor a star and launched Dimple Kapadia, and the founding text of his romantic-hero persona. Drew 62.6 million admissions in the Soviet Union, the second-best-selling film there in 1975 and the most popular Indian film of the 1970s.

title: Zehreela Insaan
source_material: Remake of Kanagal's own 1972 Kannada film Naagarahaavu which was based on three Kannada novels: Nagarahavu, Ondu Gandu Eradu Hennu and Sarpa Mathsara,
character_social_background: Village youth with a reputation for violence; guided only by his schoolmaster
role_gist: Arjun is an ill-tempered, soft-hearted young man whom the village reads as a bad character, obedient only to the schoolmaster who sees his good qualities. He loses Aarti to a forced marriage, finds a second love in his Christian classmate Margaret, and after accidentally killing the one man who understood him, asks Margaret to die with him and jumps.
principal_motivation: To be seen as something other than a bad character, and to keep the woman he loves.
principal_conflict: His own temper, and fathers on both sides who will not have him.
character_arc: From a young man whose anger is misread to one destroyed by a single unintended act of it.
character_outcome: Dies by suicide with Margaret after accidentally killing his teacher.
critical_reception: Kapoor later called the film a mistake, saying he should have taken something closer to Bobby rather than a role so drastically different.
research_notes: A remake of Puttanna Kanagal's own Kannada film Naagarahaavu (1972). Two romances are scored separately: Aarti, lost to an arranged marriage, and Margaret, who dies with him. Kapoor's own retrospective verdict on the role is recorded from the article and is the only critical comment located.

title: Raaja
producers: Sandow M. M. A. Chinnappa Thevar
research_notes: Filmography notes: Double Role. The mistaken-identity device is played on the heroine rather than on a villain: Rani cannot distinguish the twins, which is the source of most of the courtship's comedy.
character_occupation: Commoner; his twin is a CID inspector
character_social_background: One of twin brothers searching for a sister they believed dead
role_gist: Kapoor takes both twins, the ordinary Raaja and the CID inspector Ram. Raaja courts Rani, who cannot tell the brothers apart until Ram grows a moustache for her benefit, and after Ram is killed by the bandit Sher Singh's men he disguises himself as his dead brother to finish the rescue and the revenge.
principal_motivation: To recover the sister held by Sher Singh and to avenge his brother.
principal_conflict: A bandit holding his sister, and the confusion of two identical faces.
character_arc: From an untroubled commoner to a man impersonating his murdered twin to finish his work.
character_outcome: Brings the culprits to justice and marries Rani, though their sister dies of her injuries.

title: Khel Khel Mein
character_social_background: Earnest middle-class student, initially the odd one out among the pranksters
role_gist: Ajay arrives at a Shimla college as an easy target for the pranksters Vikram and Nisha, then joins them. A joke extortion note to a miserly seth is followed by the man's death, and Ajay and Nisha spend the film clearing themselves of a murder they did not commit while the real extortionist kills their friend and stalks them.
principal_motivation: To prove that a prank did not make him a murderer.
principal_conflict: A blackmailer who kills in his own name and frames the students for it.
character_arc: From a reluctant prankster to a man who has to reason his way out of a killing.
character_outcome: Clears himself and Nisha and exposes Black Cobra.
recognition: One of the defining Kapoor-Neetu Singh college comedies of the decade, and strongly identified with its R. D. Burman songs.
research_notes: Adapted from the French novel Good Children Don't Kill by Louis Thomas. The romance grows out of a three-way friendship rather than a courtship, and the thriller plot dominates the second half.

title: Rafoo Chakkar
writers: Kader Khan; Jayant Dharmadhikari; K. K. Shukla
alternate_identity: Disguises himself as the woman 'Devi' in a girls' band, and separately poses as an oil tycoon named Esso
character_social_background: Penniless performer on the run from gangsters
role_gist: Dev and his friend witness a murder, are spotted, and escape by dressing as women and joining a girls' band bound for Kashmir. In drag beside Ritu for most of the film, he courts her in a second disguise as an oil tycoon called Esso, so the romance is conducted entirely through two false identities before the men are unmasked.
principal_motivation: To stay alive, and to win Ritu while pretending to be two people he is not.
principal_conflict: The gangsters hunting him, and the impossibility of courting a woman while disguised as one.
character_arc: From a man hiding inside a disguise to one whose real identity is exposed and accepted anyway.
character_outcome: Unmasked with the romantic pairings intact; the film closes on the closing line of Some Like It Hot.
recognition: Named in the main Wikipedia article among the films that fixed Kapoor's romantic-hero image in the 1970s.
research_notes: Adapted from Some Like It Hot (1959), itself from the 1935 French film Fanfare of Love, and it keeps the American film's closing line. Deception is structural rather than malicious: the courtship depends on two simultaneous disguises.

title: Zinda Dil
alternate_identity: One of twin brothers, Arun and Kewal, played by Kapoor and a look-alike actor rather than as a double role
character_social_background: Twin son of a disabled war veteran who openly prefers the other brother
role_gist: Arun is the unfavoured twin of a war-crippled major who demands he give up everything for his brother, including the woman he loves. He leaves home, is found work by Jyoti, whose life he once saved, and discovers from a hotel waiter that the mother he believed dead is alive, which sends him back to confront his father.
principal_motivation: To be valued by a father who has always preferred his brother.
principal_conflict: A father's open favouritism and the sacrifices he demands.
character_arc: From a son who yields, including over Rekha, to one who confronts his father with the mother he hid.
character_outcome: Confronts his father with his living mother; the article leaves the resolution as a rhetorical question.
research_notes: Based on East of Eden (1955). The twin Kewal is played by the look-alike actor Rajesh Leher rather than by Kapoor, so this is not a double role. Two romances are scored: Rekha, whom he is made to renounce, and Jyoti, who takes him in afterwards.

title: Kabhie Kabhie
research_notes: Infobox gross '₹40 million' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Romance centrality is high because the film is wholly about love across two generations, but Kapoor is fifth-billed in an ensemble and his own thread is secondary to the Amit-Pooja story.
character_social_background: Son of the architect Vijay Khanna and Pooja; raised in comfort, unaware of the history between his mother and the poet Amit
role_gist: Vicky belongs to the film's younger generation, in love with his college friend Pinky. His thread turns when Pinky learns she was adopted and goes looking for her birth mother, and he is left waiting on a search that reaches back into the older couples' buried history rather than driving the film himself.
principal_motivation: To marry Pinky.
principal_conflict: Pinky's discovery of her adoption, which suspends the marriage and sends her away.
character_arc: From an uncomplicated young lover to one who has to wait out someone else's crisis of parentage.
character_outcome: Reunited with Pinky once the older generation's secrets are resolved.
recognition: A landmark Yash Chopra ensemble, and Kapoor's first major film in a cast headed by Amitabh Bachchan, Shashi Kapoor, Waheeda Rehman and Raakhee.

title: Barood
producers: J. C. Bhagat; H. S. Bhattacharya; Jitu Thakar
source_material: Based on The Summertime Killer by Antonio Isasi-Isasmendi
research_notes: Infobox gross '₹19.32 crore (US$23.52 million)' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. No rupee figures are given. The article calls it a successful venture in India and an All Time Blockbuster in the Soviet Union, where it topped the 1978 chart; the Soviet standing is recorded in recognition rather than converted into a worldwide gross. He woos Bakshi's assistant Sapna instrumentally, to get at her employer, and only Seema is scored as a romance.
character_social_background: Son of a decorated Bombay police inspector, murdered in front of him when he was eight
role_gist: Anup watches four smugglers beat his police-officer father to death on Juhu Beach at eight years old and spends twelve years preparing to kill them. The film follows him across Las Vegas, New York, Geneva and Madrid eliminating them one by one, courting Bakshi's daughter Seema partly for access, and finally surrendering himself to the detective who has shadowed him throughout.
principal_motivation: To kill the four men who murdered his father.
principal_conflict: A mafia lord hunting him while a friendly detective tries to save him from himself.
character_arc: From an orphaned boy to a methodical killer who accepts arrest once the revenge is complete.
character_outcome: Hands himself to the police after the last of the four dies, and is met by Gupta on release.
verdict: Hit in India; All Time Blockbuster in the Soviet Union
recognition: Drew about 60 million Soviet admissions, the second highest for an Indian film in the 1970s after Kapoor's own Bobby, and the fourth most successful Indian import in Soviet history.

title: Rangila Ratan
character_occupation: Small-time criminal, then a doctor's household
character_social_background: Kidnapped as a child from a government lawyer's family and raised deliberately in crime
role_gist: Kidnapped as the lawyer Dinanath's son Gopal and raised as the criminal Kishan by the man Dinanath sent to the gallows, he is groomed his whole life as an instrument of revenge against his own father. Sheltered by Dr. Anand, he is mistaken by the doctor's blind mother for her dead son Ratan and takes that name, living a third life while his foster-father hunts him.
principal_motivation: To leave the life he was raised into and keep the identity that has been offered him.
principal_conflict: The criminal foster-father who raised him as a weapon against the father he does not know he has.
character_arc: Across three names, from stolen child to criminal to a man who chooses to be Ratan.
character_outcome: The article poses the outcome as open questions and does not state the resolution.
research_notes: The article's plot section ends in rhetorical questions rather than a resolution, so the outcome and the fate of the romance with Madhu are not documented. Confidence is Low for that reason.

title: Ginny Aur Johnny

The cast list places Kapoor in a guest role without a character, among a long line of star walk-ons including Rajesh Khanna, Hema Malini, Randhir Kapoor and Vinod Mehra.

title: Laila Majnu
writers: Abrar Alvi; Anjana Rawail; H. S. Rawail
character_occupation: Son of a clan chief; later a wandering madman
character_social_background: Born to the Amari clan, hereditary enemies of Laila's Sharwaris
role_gist: Qais loves Laila from childhood with a bond so literal that a blow to one draws blood from the other. Separated by their clans, reunited as adults at a marketplace, he kills her brother in revenge for his father, is exiled, and wanders the desert as Majnu, the madman, thirsting for a single sight of her while she is married to a prince who cannot displace him.
principal_motivation: To reach Laila, and after exile simply to see her once.
principal_conflict: Two clans who would sooner be joined by blood than by love, and the killings that follow.
character_arc: From a boy who writes her name instead of God's to a man who has dissolved entirely into his love for her.
character_outcome: Dies as one of the two legendary lovers; the article records that understanding comes too late.
recognition: The best known screen Majnu of its generation and a defining entry in Kapoor's lover-boy line, carried by Madan Mohan and Jaidev's score.
research_notes: Based on the legend of Layla and Majnun. The article gives a budget of about ₹1.70 crore, a first-day take of ₹0.06 crore, ₹0.38 crore in the first week, a lifetime India nett of ₹4.25 crore and a gross of ₹8.50 crore, and calls it a blockbuster despite a modest opening.

title: Amar Akbar Anthony
writers: Kader Khan; K. K. Shukla; Jeevanprabha M. Desai; Pushpa Sharma; Prayag Raj
research_notes: Infobox gross '₹155 million' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. An ensemble of three brothers with Vinod Khanna and Amitabh Bachchan; Kapoor is second-billed and the romance with Salma is one of three parallel courtships. Named in the main Wikipedia article among the films that established his stardom.
character_social_background: The youngest of three brothers separated in childhood; raised Muslim by the tailor Darji Ilahabadi
role_gist: Akbar is the youngest of three brothers separated as children and raised in three religions, the qawwal of the trio, courting Dr. Salma Ali over the objections of her father Taiyyab Ali. He carries the film's musical register and its most famous songs, and is one of the three donors whose blood saves the blind mother none of them recognises.
principal_motivation: To marry Salma over her father's refusal, and to restore the family he does not yet know is his.
principal_conflict: A disapproving father-in-law, and a lost family scattered across three faiths.
character_arc: From a cheerful singer with a private courtship to a son restored to his mother and brothers.
character_outcome: Wins Salma and is reunited with his parents and brothers.
recognition: One of the defining masala films of Hindi cinema and among the most durable of Kapoor's 1970s credits; his qawwali numbers, above all 'Parda Hai Parda', are inseparable from the role.

title: Hum Kisise Kum Naheen
alternate_identity: Passes himself off as Manjeet Kumar Dana
character_social_background: Son of a man who died flying home with a fortune in diamonds his son never receives
role_gist: Rajesh is a hotel singer whose father dies in the air carrying a belt of diamonds meant for him. Taken in by a false story that Kishorilal has kidnapped a man's son, he sets out to trap Kishorilal's daughter Kajal by pretending to love her, and has to change course when the deception collides with her existing attachment to Sanjay.
principal_motivation: To recover his father's diamonds, initially by using Kajal.
principal_conflict: A villain manipulating him with a false kidnapping while he manipulates Kajal.
character_arc: From a man who courts a woman as a tactic to one who abandons the scheme and helps rescue her.
character_outcome: Rescues Kajal, sees her paired with Sanjay, and is paired off himself as the film closes.
recognition: Took the third spot at the 1977 box office and remains one of Nasir Hussain's best-known musicals.
research_notes: The article's plot summary is confused about which man ends with Kajal, stating both that Sanjay and Kajal become a couple and that Rajesh is paired off; the pairing row records the courtship as a deception that fails rather than asserting a marriage. Annual rank is from the article's statement that it took the third top spot at the box office in 1977.

title: Doosra Aadmi
character_social_background: Newly married young professional from a conventional middle-class family
role_gist: Karan hires Nisha, a gifted but withdrawn advertising woman still grieving a dead lover, and is drawn into a relationship with her precisely because he resembles the man she lost. Recently married to Timsy, he is the point where two claims meet: a wife who watches the attachment grow, and an older woman for whom he is a substitute rather than himself.
principal_motivation: An attraction to Nisha that he does not examine, set against the marriage he has just made.
principal_conflict: A wife on one side and, on the other, a woman who wants him for his resemblance to someone dead.
character_arc: From a young husband who thinks he can hold both to a man forced to see what he is to each of them.
character_outcome: Not documented; the article's summary stops after establishing the triangle.
research_notes: The article carries only a four-sentence plot summary that establishes the triangle and stops, so the resolution is not documented and both pairing rows are scored on the setup alone. Shashi Kapoor appears as Shashi Sehgal, the dead lover of the flashbacks, which is why his own workbook records this film as a cameo with a Tragic lovers pairing.

The article has no plot section, so the role's substance is undocumented.

title: Badaltey Rishtey
writers: Madan Joshi; Mahendra Saral; Phani Majumdar
character_social_background: Working-class guide with no money and no standing, courting a music teacher
role_gist: Manohar falls for the music teacher Savitri at first meeting and courts her by pretending to sell eggs at her door. When she is married off to the wealthy Sagar under a prediction that her husband will die within forty days, Manohar offers to kill him, reasoning that he is doomed anyway, and turns her love into hatred by befriending Sagar to prove he could do it at any moment.
principal_motivation: To have Savitri, first by courtship and then by removing her husband.
principal_conflict: A rival with money and an astrologer's prediction that he tries to turn to his own use.
character_arc: From an engaging suitor to a man whose persistence curdles into a standing threat against her husband.
character_outcome: Confronted by Sagar after Savitri exposes his intentions; the article's summary breaks off mid-scene.
research_notes: The article's plot summary breaks off in the middle of the confrontation between Manohar and Sagar, so the ending is not documented. This is the clearest early instance of a Kapoor role in which the courtship turns coercive, and it is scored accordingly rather than as a thwarted romance.

title: Sargam
source_material: Based on Siri Siri Muvva by K. Viswanath
character_social_background: Former pupil of the village schoolmaster, poor and without family standing
role_gist: Raju, a dafli player and his old teacher's former pupil, attaches himself to Hema, the schoolmaster's mute daughter, cheering her through a stepmother's campaign to keep her from dancing. When her father dies and she is thrown out, he takes her away and supports her, and the film ends with the two reunited and the stepmother reconciled.
principal_motivation: To protect Hema and to give her back the dance she is forbidden.
principal_conflict: A stepmother who resents Hema's talent, and later the vengeful Prakash.
character_arc: From a cheerful visitor who lifts her spirits to the person her survival depends on.
character_outcome: Rescued from Prakash's attack by the police and reunited with Hema.
recognition: Named in the main Wikipedia article among the films that fixed his romantic-star image; Jaya Prada's Hindi debut, reprising her role from the Telugu original.
research_notes: The Hindi version of K. Viswanath's Telugu film Siri Siri Muvva (1976). The heroine is mute, so the courtship is conducted almost entirely without her speech, which is scored in the pairing row.

title: Salaam Memsaab

title: Jhoota Kahin Ka
character_social_background: Separated from his father and brother in a shipwreck as a child; raised poor by his mother while his father became a rich man's partner
role_gist: Ajay is a lowly mechanic leading a parallel life as a lying conman and would-be Casanova, angling for the wealthy Sheetal Khanna. His habit of invention is exactly what makes him easy to frame when his estranged brother, now a murderer under another name, needs someone to carry the blame.
principal_motivation: To rise by his wits and marry money.
principal_conflict: A brother he does not recognise, plotting to pin a killing on him, and a reputation for lying that makes the frame stick.
character_arc: From a compulsive liar to a man whose lies leave him with no credible defence.
character_outcome: Framed for Mala's murder by Vikram and Prem; the article does not carry the resolution.
research_notes: The article's plot stops at the framing and does not give the outcome. character_social_background: Younger brother of Karan, living on money he believes comes from his brother's business

Two deaths and a crippling later he discovers his brother was never a businessman but a circus trapeze artist, and is a suspect in the robbery and the murder of Neeta's father.

principal_conflict: A brother's concealed life, and a police inspector's accusation that reaches into his own engagement.
character_arc: From a young man living on a comfortable fiction to one nursing a crippled brother he no longer recognises.
character_outcome: Not documented; the article's summary ends with the police inspector's revelation.

title: Gunahgaar

research_notes: Infobox gross '₹12 crore' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. Written by Khwaja Ahmad Abbas, who also wrote Shree 420 and Mera Naam Joker, so the first and the late-career film bracket the same writer. Two relationships are scored: Chandni, the fiancée he is separated from, and Henna, who loves the man with no memory and dies getting him home. The Shariat provision allowing Daroga Shahbaaz Khan two further marriages is the mechanism of the local threat to Henna.
alternate_identity: Known as 'Chand' in Pakistan while amnesiac; credited as Chandar Prakash / Chand
character_occupation: Kashmiri from Srinagar; works making clay pots while amnesiac
character_social_background: An Indian Hindu from Srinagar, engaged to Chandni Kaul, who wakes with no memory in Pakistani Kashmir
role_gist: Chandar is engaged to Chandni when a car accident carries him across the line of control into Pakistan with no memory of who he is. Nursed by Henna and her family, called Chand after the name he cries in his sleep, he is loved by her and about to marry her when his memory returns on the wedding day and reveals that he is neither Muslim nor Pakistani.
principal_motivation: First to recover an identity he has lost, and then to get home without destroying the family that saved him.
principal_conflict: A border, two religions, a police officer who wants Henna for himself, and a suspicion that he is an Indian spy.
character_arc: From a bridegroom to a man with no name, and back to himself at the exact moment that knowledge becomes catastrophic.
character_outcome: Reaches India on the second attempt at the cost of Henna's life; the article records the film ending with him asking why there must be war.
recognition: The project Raj Kapoor had planned and begun before his death, completed by Rishi's brother Randhir Kapoor, and notable for casting the Pakistani actress Zeba Bakhtiar in the title role.

title: Ranbhoomi
character_occupation: Not documented; a villager newly arrived in the city
character_social_background: Village-born, simple-minded and honest, with five hundred rupees to his name
role_gist: Bholanath comes to the city with five hundred rupees and, thinking his money safer with her than with himself, leaves it with a prostitute. He then attaches himself to the gangster Roopa, keeps house for him, and when Roopa's war with a rival gangster escalates offers himself as the hostage that might end it.
principal_motivation: To end the hostilities between the two gangsters by putting himself in the middle of them.
principal_conflict: Two gang bosses, neither of whom has any reason to value his life.
character_arc: From a naive villager to a man who stakes himself on a gangster's capacity for loyalty.
character_outcome: Not documented; the article's plot ends on whether Roopa will compromise to save him and whether Chandan will let him live.

title: Banjaran
character_occupation: Son of the landowner Rana Udaybhan Singh Sesodia
character_social_background: Aristocratic landowning family, on whose land the nomadic Banjara tribe camps
role_gist: Kumar Singh feels an unaccountable pull towards Reshma, a Banjara girl camped on his father's land, and her recurring nightmare of being hunted to death stops the moment he arrives. Both families oppose them, she is promised elsewhere, and they run away to an old haveli, where the caretaker reveals that they are the reborn Devi and Suraj, killed the first time for the same love.
principal_motivation: To be with Reshma against both fathers.
principal_conflict: His own father's objection to a nomad girl, her father's prior engagement of her, and the armed men both bring.
character_arc: From a landowner's son drawn to a stranger to one half of a couple completing a love interrupted by murder a generation earlier.
character_outcome: United with Reshma after Thakur Baba's account of their previous lives ends the feud.
research_notes: The third Kapoor and Sridevi pairing, after Nagina (1986) and Chandni (1989), and the second reincarnation romance of his career after Karz, though here the previous life belongs to both partners rather than to him alone. The resolution is unusual in that the man who killed the lovers in their first life is the one who pleads for them in the second.

title: Kasak
source_material: Based on Mouna Ragam by Mani Ratnam
character_occupation: Not documented; the prospective groom of an arranged match
character_social_background: A suitable match produced by Divya's father, with no history in her life
role_gist: Vijay is the groom of an arranged marriage to a woman still grieving the revolutionary she loved and watched die. He waits out her rudeness, marries her when her father's heart attack forces her hand, does not touch her, listens to the whole of her history, and then offers her a choice between the divorce she asked for as a wedding gift and the anklets he bought her. She chooses divorce, and the law makes them live together for a year.
principal_motivation: To be chosen by a woman who has already told him she does not want him.
principal_conflict: A wife in love with a dead man, and a marriage neither the law nor her family will let her leave.
character_arc: From a patient suitor to a husband who offers the divorce rather than extract a consent, and then has a year in which to be preferred.
character_outcome: Not documented in full; the article's plot breaks off during the year the couple are compelled to share.
research_notes: A remake of Mani Ratnam's Tamil film Mouna Ragam. Neelam is top-billed and the film is hers; Kapoor plays the husband whose restraint is the story's moral centre. This is one of the very few roles in the filmography in which he neither courts nor pursues, and it produces the highest relationship-health reading of any strained marriage in the career.

character_social_background: Ran away from home as a boy to escape his father's beatings and grew up a thief, unaware his elder brother is now wealthy

He confesses, takes the pregnant and disowned Sharda back to their village, and recognises from a portrait whose brother he is.

character_occupation: Wealthy young man of the Sahai-adjacent business family
character_social_background: Rich and handsome only son of Lakshmi Devi, and heir to a fortune his uncle and cousin are next in line for
role_gist: Ravi marries Kajal with his mother's blessing and is thrown off a cliff for it by relatives who stand to inherit. Presumed dead, he leaves her a widow; he survives, and returns to find that she has remarried and that her new husband has become his friend. The film's second half is built on his existence being the obstacle to a marriage he has no wish to break.
principal_motivation: To marry Kajal, and after his return to avoid destroying what she has rebuilt.
principal_conflict: A greedy uncle who tried to kill him, and a second marriage his survival invalidates.
character_arc: From an untroubled bridegroom to a man whose being alive is a problem for the woman he loves.
character_outcome: Kidnapped with Kajal and Raja by Dhirendra, who demands his property; the article's plot breaks off there.
recognition: Shah Rukh Khan's feature-film debut, in which he plays the second husband; among the most commercially successful films of Kapoor's later leading-man period, and inseparable from its Nadeem-Shravan score.
critical_reception: The article records Kapoor crediting Nadeem-Shravan's music rather than himself for the film's success, and cites a reviewer praising the performances of Kapoor and Bharti. Rachit Gupta of Filmfare wrote in 2014 that Divya Bharti seemed at ease sharing screen space with him.

title: Bol Radha Bol
research_notes: Filmography notes: Double Role. The double role is played by Kapoor as both Kishan and Tony Montana, and Juhi Chawla is credited as Radha / Rita, so both leads are doubled. The romance is threatened not by a rival for Radha's affection but by a man wearing her lover's face, which is why it is classified as manipulated by outsiders.
character_social_background: Wealthy head of a business house, with a mother, an uncle and a defrauding cousin
role_gist: Kishan goes to a village on business, teaches Radha English and falls in love with her, and returns home to find his mother dead and an exact double installed in his place who knows everything about him, including Radha. His dog goes to the impostor, he is thrown out of his own house and arrested at his own office, and has to prove his identity from outside it.
principal_motivation: To recover his own name, his house and Radha.
principal_conflict: A double who has taken his identity, backed by the cousin he banished.
character_arc: From an industrialist secure in everything to a man with no proof he is himself, and then to the one person who can expose the substitution.
character_outcome: Escapes custody, reaches Radha, and traces the impostor to Goa, where he learns the man's name is Tony Montana.
critical_reception: The article records the film as the tenth highest-grossing film of the year.

title: Shreemaan Aashique
character_social_background: Nephew of Professor Vishwamitra, who runs an association of confirmed bachelors, and son of parents anxious to see him married
role_gist: Dushyant has promised his uncle, who presides over an association of confirmed single men, that he will never marry. Shakuntala falls in love with him on a hill-station holiday and he rebuffs her; she persists until he returns the feeling, which sets him against the uncle whose creed he has broken and who then falls in love with Shakuntala himself.
principal_motivation: To keep a vow of bachelorship he no longer believes in, and then to keep Shakuntala instead.
principal_conflict: An uncle who extracted the vow and becomes a rival for the same woman.
character_arc: From a man defined by a promise never to marry to one who breaks it against the person he made it to.
character_outcome: Ends with Shakuntala, according to the article.
research_notes: The courtship runs in reverse of the usual pattern for Kapoor: the woman pursues and he resists, which makes this one of the few films in the filmography where the initiative is hers throughout. The uncle's rivalry is what turns the comedy into a triangle.

title: Damini
producers: Karim Morani; Bunty Soorma; Aly Morani
research_notes: Infobox gross '₹ 11.75 crore' has no nett/gross label and is not entered. character_occupation: Elder son of the industrialist Kedarnath Gupta; works in the family business
character_social_background: Wealthy industrial family, married across a wide class gap to a lower-middle-class woman
role_gist: Shekhar falls in love with Damini at a charity performance and marries her across a sharp class divide. When she witnesses his younger brother and his friends gang-raping the family's maid, Shekhar runs to stop it and arrives too late, and then spends the film caught between a wife determined to testify and a family determined to bury it. He objects to what his family does to her and never quite acts against them.
principal_motivation: To keep both his wife and his family, when the two become incompatible.
principal_conflict: A family covering up a rape, and a wife whose conscience will not let her join the cover-up.
character_arc: From an ardent husband to a man whose decency is exhausted by objecting, while his wife is committed to an institution on his family's lawyer's motion.
character_outcome: Not documented in full; the article records him becoming upset with his family while the Guptas and Bajaj reconcile, and Damini escaping the institution alone.
recognition: One of the best-known Hindi films about sexual violence and the courts, and among the most substantial films of Kapoor's later leading period; the title role and Sunny Deol's lawyer are what the film is remembered for.

title: Eena Meena Deeka
character_social_background: A man robbing banks to pay for his mother's medical treatment, and unknowingly the younger brother of the ex-convict he entangles

Forced to flee together, Eena refuses to confess and runs off, and is revealed to be the brother Deeka lost to a kidnapping in childhood.

title: Saajan Ka Ghar
writers: Aadesh K. Arjun; Keshav Rathod; Dhirendra Bohra
source_material: Remake of 1983 Gujarati movie Mahiyar Ni Chundadi
character_social_background: Son of a household headed by a mother who turns murderous towards his wife; married to a woman her own family despises
role_gist: Amar, an army officer, is married to Laxmi by the father and stepmother who have mistreated her since birth. After her miscarriage he is told she will die if she carries another pregnancy to term, and decides to tell nobody, including her. She overhears, resolves to have a child even if it kills her, and provokes him into a night he is horrified by; he then leaves for duty rather than consult a doctor, and his mother throws her out of the house.
principal_motivation: To spare Laxmi the knowledge that a pregnancy would kill her.
principal_conflict: A fatal medical fact he conceals, and a mother who decides to murder his wife for not conceiving.
character_arc: From a husband protecting his wife by silence to one whose silence produces exactly the pregnancy that will kill her, and who leaves rather than face it.
character_outcome: Not documented in full; he departs for duty and the article follows Laxmi, thrown out of the house and sleeping in a barn.
research_notes: Juhi Chawla is first-billed and the film is Laxmi's. The concealment is the plot's engine and the article is explicit about its consequence: rather than consult a doctor or discuss an abortion, Amar goes off to duty. That judgement is recorded in the pairing row rather than softened, and it places this among the group of 1990s roles in which Kapoor plays husbands who fail their wives at the decisive moment.

title: Pehla Pehla Pyar
source_material: Based on Roman Holiday by Dalton Trumbo
character_social_background: Outside Sapna's aristocratic world; the man she lands on after running away from it
role_gist: Raj takes in a runaway he initially wants rid of. Sapna has fled an aristocratic household she found intolerable, and his first instinct is to get her off his hands; instead he falls in love with her, and when her family posts a reward for information on her whereabouts the two of them have to go on the run together.
principal_motivation: First to be rid of an inconvenient runaway, and then to keep her out of her family's reach.
principal_conflict: An aristocratic family that puts a price on locating her and the flight that follows.
character_arc: From a man trying to hand a stranger back to the family she escaped to one running from it beside her.
character_outcome: Not documented; the article's summary ends with the couple on the run.
research_notes: The article records the film as loosely inspired by Roman Holiday, and its plot prose sits under a Summary heading rather than a Plot one, which is why the extraction script reported no plot section for it; the text was recovered by hand and the role and pairing are written from it. Amrish Puri and Gulshan Grover play the aristocratic household's enforcers. The reluctant-man-and-runaway structure inverts the usual Kapoor courtship, in which he is the pursuer.

title: Prem Yog
alternate_identity: Lives in Bombay as the waiter Raju rather than as the Yuvraj of Ramgarh
character_occupation: Heir to the throne of Ramgarh; works as a waiter in Bombay
character_social_background: Only son of Maharaj Chhatrapal Singh, raised in seclusion inside the palace on an astrologer's prediction that he would never inherit a throne
role_gist: Raju is kept inside his father's palace all his life because an astrologer predicted the throne would end with his father. Unwilling to accept the marriage arranged for him, he runs away to Bombay with his bodyguard, works as a waiter, and falls in love with the singer Anita, who is angry when a rival reveals that he is an heir he never told her about.
principal_motivation: To live outside the palace and marry the woman he chose rather than the one chosen for him.
principal_conflict: A father who arrives with an army to fetch him, and a concealed identity that costs him Anita's trust.
character_arc: From a prince kept in seclusion to a waiter who has to decide whether to be captured or keep running.
character_outcome: Not documented; the article ends with Raju facing the choice between capture and flight.
research_notes: The article records the film as heavily inspired by Coming to America. Shammi Kapoor plays his father, one of several films pairing them as father and son. The concealment of his rank, rather than the rank itself, is what ruptures the romance, which makes this a variation on the false-identity courtships of the 1970s films.

title: Ghar Ki Izzat
source_material: Based on Banga Kora
character_occupation: Becomes a famous singer; earlier without independent occupation
character_social_background: One of four brothers in a joint family held together by the eldest, Ram Kumar
role_gist: Mohan is the brother who bickers with and loves Geeta, his sister-in-law's younger sister and a child widow living in the household. When two incoming wives break the family's solidarity and denounce Geeta publicly as a widow, she is sent away to be tormented at her in-laws'; Mohan follows the collapsing family to the village, becomes a singer to support them, and the film ends with their marriage.
principal_motivation: To marry Geeta and hold what is left of the family together.
principal_conflict: Two sisters-in-law who destroy the joint household and use Geeta's widowhood as a weapon.
character_arc: From one of four brothers in a shared house to the earner who supports the family and marries the widow it discarded.
character_outcome: Rescues Shyam and Mona from Sheetal's plot, reunites the family, and marries Geeta.
recognition: The third film in the filmography built on widow remarriage, after Prem Rog (1982) and Deewana (1992).

Geeta is described as a child widow, which makes this the third widow-remarriage plot of Kapoor's career and the second in which he marries the widow himself.

principal_conflict: Her father's prior arrangement with the family of Sagar's own childhood friend.
